links.reading: William, your deep concern can help Charlotte feel cared for, and her warmth can make it easier for you to show it. She may respond well when you stay close without taking over. At bedtime, let affection be simple and let her decide how much to say. Behaviour check: Notice whether Charlotte talks more when you listen without pressing.

William, your practical help can get Charlotte moving when homework feels difficult. She may enjoy joining you when she can choose the first step. Keep the help small, rather than doing the task for her. This gives her practice starting on her own. Behaviour check: At the kitchen table, ask Charlotte which part she wants to try first.

William, you may want to end a disagreement by setting a firm limit. Charlotte may hold on to her view when she feels pushed. This is the challenge: keep the limit, but let her tell you what feels unfair. That helps her learn to disagree without fearing your answer. Behaviour check: During one disagreement, hear her reason before repeating the rule.

William, a clear instruction may still leave Charlotte unsure what you meant, especially during the morning rush. She may nod before she has understood. Ask her to tell you the next step in her own words. This gives both of you a chance to catch confusion without blame. Behaviour check: Give one instruction, then ask Charlotte what she heard.

William, you may offer more comfort than Charlotte has asked for, while she may avoid saying what she wants. A gentle guess can miss the mark. Ask before stepping in, and accept a short answer. That helps her practise naming what feels good to her. Behaviour check: When she seems quiet, ask whether she wants company or time alone.

William, you may change the plan quickly, while Charlotte needs time to work out what you mean. In the morning rush, a sudden change can leave her unsure what to do first. Say what has changed and give her one next step. This helps her adjust without guessing. Behaviour check: Change one plan this week and ask Charlotte to repeat the next step.

William, your steady limits can help Charlotte take on a job without feeling she must do everything. She can bring enthusiasm when the task is clear and manageable. Agree on what she will do and when it will be finished. That helps her learn to keep a promise at her own pace. Behaviour check: Choose one small job and agree on its finish time together.

William, you may want a plan to stay fixed, while Charlotte may want to change it once she has started. Neither of you needs to turn that difference into a contest. Set the necessary limit, then offer a choice inside it. This helps her practise freedom while keeping an agreement. Behaviour check: Let Charlotte choose when to stop within the tablet limit.

William, Charlotte may feel your concern strongly, even when you have not said much. At bedtime, she may need time before she can explain what upset her. Stay nearby without demanding an answer. Your patience helps her learn that difficult feelings can be spoken safely. Behaviour check: Ask one gentle question at bedtime, then wait for Charlotte's answer.

William, you may help Charlotte adjust to a new routine, while she may be cautious about changing what works. A sudden change can unsettle her, but a clear reason and steady follow-through help. Tell her what will stay the same as well as what will change. Behaviour check: Before changing one routine, ask Charlotte what part she wants to keep.

Charlotte, you bring your effort into William's daily jobs. He may notice how you handle small tasks and invite you to help. At your age, a clear job can feel good when it has a fair limit. Behaviour check: Choose one manageable job together and agree when it will be done.

Charlotte, your feelings can shape how William experiences friends, groups, and shared plans. He may value having you alongside him, while you may want to know where you belong. A Sunday call can give you both an easy way to connect. Behaviour check: Ask William what he enjoyed about the call, then share your own answer.

William, you are present in Charlotte's sense of who she is. Your attention can encourage her, but she may also watch your face closely for approval. Let her see that you can listen without deciding for her. That helps her practise trusting her own view. Behaviour check: Ask Charlotte what she thinks before you give your opinion.

William, you bring strong direction into Charlotte's home life. She may feel it most when you set rules about her room or daily routines. Keep the rule clear and explain the one job you expect. This helps her understand what she can decide for herself. Behaviour check: Agree on one room job and let Charlotte choose when to do it.
